summary: Frontend-only E2E test of the Ganapati Modak Dash upgrade (3-level demon chase). Verified: menu (title + PLAY/HOW TO PLAY/BEST SCORE/SETTINGS), all 3 panels open/close, PLAY starts Level 1, HUD contains hud-level ('LEVEL 1'), chase progress bar, hud-score, hud-distance, 3 hud-lives, blessing-meter. 3D scene renders correctly: horned Demon (Rakshasa) is running ahead on the road, Ganesha is seen from behind (facing forward), Himalayan mountains backdrop visible. Controls (ArrowLeft/Right/Up/Space/Down, KeyE) fire without console errors. Score/distance both increase. Obstacles are placed by the demon on the road (large stone visible mid-play). OUCH toast fires on collision, blessing meter fills, 2x GOLDEN and FLOWER SHOWER events proc, combo increments (x16 achieved). Game Over screen (data-testid=gameover-screen) appears with all stats (Distance, Modaks Collected, Highest Combo, Final Score, Personal Best) plus NEW PERSONAL BEST banner and PLAY AGAIN + MAIN MENU buttons. PLAY AGAIN restarts (HUD reappears). MAIN MENU returns to main menu. Local leaderboard persists across full page reload (localStorage key 'ganapati_modak_dash_v1'); BEST SCORE panel shows Best Score / Highest Combo / Longest Distance / Total Modaks / Runs Played matching the stored value; menu's 'Best: <n>' updates. Cinematic letterbox and ending screen elements are wired in JSX (data-testid=letterbox, stage-banner, ending-screen, ending-message, btn-ending-again, btn-ending-menu) but the Level 1 -> catch -> escape -> Level 2 auto-advance transition could NOT be fully observed inside the automation browser due to requestAnimationFrame throttling: distance accumulates at ~0.8-1.2 m/s in the headless test env (Level 1 target is 500m, so it would need ~7-10 min of continuous play, not the 60-120s expected). This is an environment limitation, not a bug — the code path (chase.js _beginCatch/_beginEscape/triggerEnding, Game.startRun(levelIndex), GanapatiDash onEvent handlers for CATCH/ESCAPE/LEVEL/ENDING_TRIGGER, cinematic letterbox conditional, stage-banner) is correctly wired and static review shows the flow will fire when target is reached.
action_items: Consider exposing the Game instance to window in a debug/testing mode (e.g., window.__gmd = this in Game constructor when a URL flag is present) so future automated tests can fast-forward chase.levelDist for verifying Level 1 -> Level 2 -> Level 3 -> ending cinematics without waiting for real-time distance. This is optional/QA-only.

OPTIONAL: On slow render envs (headless CI), the dt clamp of 0.05 (max) at Game.js:677 combined with real fps of ~4-5 makes the game effectively run at ~1/5 real speed. Not a bug on real hardware; only impacts automated E2E for the level auto-advance. Consider making the clamp configurable or adding a small `?turbo=1` debug flag that scales levelSpeedMul for CI.
critical_code_review_comments: GanapatiDash.jsx remains ~540 lines mixing engine wiring, HUD, panels, toasts, input, and multiple overlays. Suggest extracting HUD, PanelOverlay, Toasts, GameOverScreen, EndingScreen into dedicated components for maintainability (still valid from iteration_1).

Game.js is ~1310 lines and is doing scene setup, spawn logic, chase orchestration, particles hookups, audio, camera, and update loop. Splitting into GameCore, SpawnManager, CameraRig, EventScheduler modules would improve testability.

chase.js: LEVELS[].target values (500/700/900) combined with distance accumulation of `effSpeed * dt * 0.8` mean Level 1 takes roughly 40-50s of real-world play at unclamped 60fps and speed 13. That matches the request's '60-120s per level' expectation, but on any slower/throttled tab it scales linearly. Consider capping level progress by game time as a fallback (min of time-based and distance-based) so the auto-advance still fires within a bounded interval.
Storage.getSettings still returns the default object on parse-success without merging (from iteration_1). New settings added later will be missing keys from any pre-existing save.
touchmove listener attached as { passive: false } even when not in the 'playing' state (from iteration_1) — micro-optimization.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for all observable flows; Level-catch/Level-2/ending transitions not reachable inside headless env due to rAF throttling

context_for_next_testing_agent: In the automation browser, distance accumulates at ~1 m/s (dt clamp + slow render) so reaching Level 1's 500m target takes ~8-10 minutes of continuous key input. If retesting the catch/escape/Level-2/ending, either (a) run 8-10 min of active input while pressing occasional keys to prevent throttling, (b) ask main agent to add a temporary window.__gmd debug handle so tests can bump chase.levelDist directly, or (c) verify manually. All static wiring (chase._beginCatch -> onEvent('CATCH'), _beginEscape -> onEvent('ESCAPE') + stage banner, triggerEnding -> onEvent('ENDING_TRIGGER')) is confirmed present. data-testids used: main-menu, btn-play, btn-howto, btn-scores, btn-settings, panel-howto, panel-scores, panel-settings, panel-close, hud, hud-level, hud-score, hud-distance, hud-lives, blessing-meter, blessing-activate, hud-combo, hud-golden, game-toast, letterbox, stage-banner, gameover-screen, btn-play-again, btn-main-menu, ending-screen, ending-message, btn-ending-again, btn-ending-menu, new-best. LocalStorage key is 'ganapati_modak_dash_v1'.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs observed. The only observability gap (Level 1 -> catch -> Level 2 -> ending cinematic) is caused by the automation browser's low frame rate combined with Game.js:677 `if (dt > 0.05) dt = 0.05;` clamp: when the tab is running at ~4-5 fps in the headless env, real-world distance rate drops to ~1 m/s making the 500m target take ~8 min instead of ~60s. On real user hardware this is not a problem.
